artists.biography:
LONELY ROBOT is a British Crossover Prog solo project from journeyman guitarist John MITCHELL. MITCHELL joined the progressive scene as the guitar player for supergroup ARENA in 1997. He had a big set of shoes to fill as he replaced outgoing Keith MORE (ASIA) but has done more than adequately remaining a mainstay with the band throughout their heyday, holding his own while trading solos off with prog legend Clive NOLAN (PENDRAGON). While maintaining his commitment to ARENA, MITCHELL continued to build his prog resume with THE URBANE, John WETTON (ASIA, KING CRIMSON), KINO, FROST*, IT BITES and most recently GALDALF'S FIST. In addition to his impressive guitar work, MITCHELL was also the lead singer for KINO and IT BITES.

In 2014, MITCHELL decided it was time to do his own project. On the Inside Out record label's announcement, MITCHELL stated:

''I'd long thought about doing an album where I could have total control from start to finish with the music, lyrics, production, and choosing who I wanted to contribute - expanding from the idea of just a solo album. Musically, this album is very proggy, but more about atmosphere than technical expertise, inspired by my love of science fiction and interest in the evolution of the human race.''

perplexity.description:
A Model Life is the fifth studio album by Lonely Robot, the solo project masterminded by producer, guitarist, and vocalist John Mitchell (known for It Bites and Frost), released on August 26, 2022, via Inside Out Music and Sony Music. Marking Mitchell’s most honest and vulnerable record to date, the album blends melodic progressive rock with soft rock sensibilities, drawing echoes of Peter Gabriel and Roger Waters in Mitchell’s vocal delivery while incorporating cinematic synth textures and a notable return of the guitar solo . The ten-track collection, including songs like “Recalibrating,” “Digital God Machine,” and “Duty Of Care,” navigates themes of 21st-century alienation, broken relationships, personal grief, and the struggle to maintain mental and physical well-being in turbulent times .

Musically, A Model Life is rarely overtly progressive in a traditional sense; instead, it functions as a superior soft rock record infused with grit, subtle key changes, and lush, immersive production . Critics have hailed it as Mitchell’s crowning achievement and the most complete, cohesive release from Lonely Robot, revealing its full depth only after multiple listens . The album balances personal introspection with an objective look at the world, offering a profoundly emotional yet uplifting soundtrack that avoids being unpolished or purely melancholic . With Craig Blundell on drums and Mitchell’s signature multi-instrumental prowess, A Model Life stands as a masterfully crafted, accessible, and deeply human work that defines the essence of the Lonely Robot project .
